Per Dokploy's own comparison, Preview Deployments are offered only by Dokploy and Coolify; CapRover and Dokku lack preview environments entirely, and CapRover/Dokku also lack Docker Compose support.
quote: Only Dokploy and Coolify offer this feature. CapRover and Dokku lack preview environment support entirely ... Dokploy includes Docker Compose support, while CapRover and Dokku do not

claim: Coolify offers native per-branch deploy support with isolated environments at unique subdomains; Dokku needs a plugin and manual config for multi-env, while Kamal and CapRover lack native preview functionality; install times on Debian/Ubuntu are ~30 min (Coolify, curl+UI), ~20 min (Dokku CLI), ~20 min (CapRover docker run), ~15 min (Kamal YAML); Kamal is a deploy tool not a PaaS with no server abstraction.
quote: Coolify leads with "native per-branch deploy support" ... Dokku requires a plugin and manual configuration for multi-environment setups ... Kamal and CapRover both lack native preview functionality ... Kamal is a deploy tool ... no server abstraction layer

claim: Dokploy supports multi-server natively via Docker Swarm with automatic Traefik routing across the cluster, and reports lower idle CPU (~0.8%) than Coolify (~6%+).
quote: Dokploy uses 0.8% idle CPU vs Coolify 6%+ ... Dokploy supports multi-server natively via Docker Swarm ... Traefik automatically detects your running containers and routes traffic to them across the cluster

claim: Komodo is a self-hosted fleet/container management platform (Rust backend, Periphery agents) with build pipelines from Git and compose-stack deployment across servers — positioned as a Portainer alternative with built-in CI/CD, not a Vercel-style PR-preview PaaS.
quote: Komodo is built for fleet management with a Rust backend, Periphery agents, build pipelines from Git ... can be thought of as a Portainer alternative with built-in CI/CD capabilities
